# 1 Clement Chapter 59 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 59 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_059_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 59

*[The Great Prayer — Part I: Opening Address and Petition for Illumination]*

**59:1** If there are those who refuse to obey what he has said through us, let them understand that they are tangling themselves in sin and no small danger. As for us — we will be free from this offense, and we will pray with earnest supplication that the Creator of all things will keep intact the full count of his chosen ones throughout the whole world, through his beloved child Jesus Christ. Through Christ he has called us from darkness into light, from ignorance into the knowledge of the glory of his name.

**59:2** *Grant us to hope in your name — the name that is the very origin of all creation.*
*Open the eyes of our hearts to know you:*
*you who alone are the Most High among all heights,*
*the Holy One dwelling among the holy.*

*You humble the arrogance of the proud.*
*You scatter the plans of nations.*
*You lift up the lowly and bring down the lofty.*
*You make rich and make poor.*
*You kill and you make alive.*

*You alone are the Discoverer of spirits*
*and the God of all flesh.*
*You look into the depths;*
*you observe all that human beings do.*

*You are the Helper of those in danger,*
*the Savior of those in despair,*
*the Creator and Keeper of every spirit.*

*You multiply the peoples of the earth,*
*and from all of them you have chosen those who love you*
*through Jesus Christ, your beloved child —*
*through whom you have taught us,*
*made us holy,*
*and honored us.*

**59:3** *We beg you, Master — be our helper and defender.*
*Save those among us who are suffering.*
*Raise up the lowly.*
*Lift up those who have fallen.*
*Heal the sick.*
*Bring back the wanderers from your people.*
*Feed the hungry.*
*Free the captives.*
*Strengthen the weak.*
*Give courage to the despondent.*

*Let all the nations know you —*
*that you alone are God,*
*that Jesus Christ is your child,*
*and that we are your people,*
*the sheep of your pasture.*

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity, with chs. 59–61 laid out as liturgical poetry to honor their character as one of the earliest Christian prayers.*
